title: BackTech Elite
subtitle: A large-laptop backpack built around a load-bearing TPU frame
role: Research, concept, frame testing, pattern making and sample making
summary: BackTech Elite is a computer backpack I designed in 2023 for carrying a heavy laptop over 16 inches along with its power adapter and accessories. This piece was about staying inside one narrow category and one small, specific need, then looking for an interesting answer. Because a backpack is partly a fashion object, I wanted to handle real back load without accepting a heavy, bulky look.

sections.heading: A narrow, heavy problem
sections.body:
The need showed up plainly around me. People left expensive laptops in open, unattended classrooms, or stayed late to finish heavy work so they would not have to carry the computer home on foot or by bicycle.

Asking 50 people in computer science, industrial design and engineering confirmed how narrow and real the load was. Almost all of them used laptops over 16 inches, carrying an average of 4 kg over commutes longer than 20 minutes. Existing bags large enough for those machines suffered from complicated layering, weak protection and flush back panels with no real carrying system.

sections.heading: Moving load off the shoulders
sections.body:
I spent serious time studying how the back takes weight and how to route that load to the right place to take pressure off the shoulders and body. After reviewing carrying-system patents and research on shoulder straps, back cushions and hip support, I built frame and strap mock-ups and tested them on 20 people of different heights and weights.

The first frame was too large, the second pressed into the lower back with too little flexibility, and a triangular support stressed the hip. Magnetic straps and retractable back straps wore poorly too. Resting support on the upper gluteal surface let a streamlined TPU frame transfer load to the waist and hips while keeping air space between the back and the protected laptop compartment.

sections.heading: Lightening a heavy silhouette
sections.body:
A bag built for a very heavy computer usually looks large and heavy. Because a backpack also sits close to fashion, I used a translucent outer layer so daylight and outside light pass into the shell, letting the whole pack look lighter. Bright orange appears as a single accent, leaving material contrast to do the rest.

Inside, the pack separates into three zones, placing the water bottle and umbrella storage at the bottom so liquids stay away from electronics.

sections.heading: Sewing my first fabric piece
sections.body: From sketches I made a paper mock-up, built the parts in 3D software, printed flat patterns onto cardboard, and sewed the final sample myself. This was my first backpack and my first soft-fabric object. Working through revisions taught me hemming, hardware placement and stitches directly through making mistakes.
